title: Storage Anatomy: Sectors to Partitions 💾
description: Understand how hard drives and SSDs organize data physically and logically, from platters to partition tables.

slides.title: Physical vs Logical Storage 🧊
slides.content:
# The Layers of a Drive

A storage device has multiple layers:

- **Physical**: Platters, tracks, sectors (on HDD); flash cells (on SSD).
- **Logical**: How the OS sees the drive – a linear array of **Logical Block Addresses (LBAs)**.

Historically, a **sector** was 512 bytes, but modern drives may use 4096‑byte (4K) sectors. The OS still sees 512‑byte emulation sometimes.

quizData.question: What is the traditional sector size for most hard drives?
quizData.explanation: 512 bytes per sector has been the standard for decades, though newer drives use 4096‑byte sectors.

slides.title: Clusters (Allocation Units) 📦
slides.content:
## Where Efficiency Meets Waste

The OS doesn’t allocate one sector at a time – it groups sectors into **clusters** (also called allocation units).

- FAT32: cluster size can be up to 32 KB.
- NTFS: typically 4 KB (4K) but configurable.

A 1‑byte file still consumes one whole cluster. The unused space inside that cluster is **file slack** – a goldmine for forensics.

quizData.question: A 3 KB file on a file system with 4 KB clusters will occupy exactly 3 KB on disk.
quizData.explanation: It occupies one full 4 KB cluster; the remaining 1 KB is slack space that may contain old data.

slides.title: Partition Tables 📊
slides.content:
## Splitting the Drive

A drive can be divided into partitions, each with its own file system. The partition table tells the OS where each begins and ends.

- **MBR (Master Boot Record)**: Old standard, located in the first sector (LBA 0). Can hold up to 4 primary partitions. Uses 32‑bit LBA, limited to 2 TB.
- **GPT (GUID Partition Table)**: Modern, part of UEFI. Uses 64‑bit LBAs, supports huge drives, stores backup header at end of disk.

From a forensic perspective, the partition table is the first thing you examine.

slides.title: View MBR with dd + xxd
slides.content: Extract the first sector (512 bytes) to see the MBR and partition entries.
slides.codeSnippet:
dd if=/dev/sda of=mbr.bin bs=512 count=1
xxd mbr.bin | less  # Scroll to 0x1BE for partition entries.

quizData.question: Which partition table scheme supports disks larger than 2 TB?
quizData.explanation: GPT uses 64‑bit addressing, allowing it to handle drives much larger than 2 TB.

slides.title: Volume Boot Record (VBR) 🚀
slides.content:
Each partition starts with a VBR (also called boot sector). It contains:
- Jump instruction to boot code.
- BIOS Parameter Block (BPB): describes the file system (bytes per sector, sectors per cluster, etc.).
- Signature `55 AA` at offset 510‑511.

If the VBR is damaged, the partition may appear unformatted. Forensics can reconstruct it.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Check for Host Protected Areas (HPA) and Device Configuration Overlays (DCO)

Drives can hide a small area from the OS, used by manufacturers – or by criminals to stash evidence. Tools like `hdparm` can detect and remove HPA/DCO.
